items.headline: Quantum Leap Energy and Necsa sign heads of agreement for South African HALEU plant
items.what_happened: Quantum Leap Energy (QLE) and South Africa's state nuclear company Necsa signed a heads of agreement to form a joint venture that would develop, build and operate a commercial-scale HALEU facility at Necsa's Pelindaba site. QLE would hold about 80% and Necsa about 20%. QLE says it has already secured offtake for the output through supply agreements with TerraPower.
items.why_it_matters: It is a new non-US source of HALEU, one of the fuel bottlenecks for advanced reactors. For a 1-20 MW buyer it is still years away, and the stated output is already committed to TerraPower.
items.binding_note: A heads of agreement. The release calls the agreement a binding commercial framework for the joint venture, but no final investment decision, construction start or licence is announced in the sources read.
